rv.q: Lack of power, however, is no way to describe In the Heights, which ignited a new energy source for musical theater last night at the Theatre.
Its fundamental deficiencies are also along for the ride, unfortunately.

Miranda and Quiara Alegría Hudes have rendered a simple and not at all offensive world, and brought little that is new to the familiar Broadway spectacle of earnest, smiling immigrants singing and dancing for our delectation.
But reality is not the issue here; rather, it is fantasy, music, singing and dancing, and some salty dialogue, as well as flawless production values and performance.
All the tweaking has turned the evening into an immensely satisfying experience that is sure to charm even the most entrenched cynic.

I love the idea of In the Heights, and I think Miranda's voice as performer and writer needs to be heard on the NYC stage. But this show is a jumble of ideas, some of them interesting, many others quite mundane or cliched. In the Heights has got a beat; it's got energy. But it's finally so much less than it ought to have been!

cn.t: Critics embrace Lin-Manuel Miranda's vibrant musical as an infectious celebration of Latino culture in Washington Heights, praising its energetic blend of hip-hop, salsa, and merengue with strong performances and production values.

vs.sum: The Richard Rodgers offers strong sightlines from most orchestra and front mezzanine seats, with good acoustics for musicals. However, legroom is notably tight throughout, especially in the orchestra, and rear mezzanine seats feel distant from the stage.

acc.note: Stair lift to orchestra; elevator to mezzanine. Inductive hearing loop installed.
